title: Fraction Calculation Methodology
overview: Fractions represent parts of a whole. Understanding fraction operations, simplification using GCD, and conversion between formats is fundamental to mathematics.

methods.name: Fraction Operations
methods.description: The four basic operations on fractions: addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division.

formula.name: Fraction Arithmetic
formula.expression:
Addition: a/b + c/d = (ad + bc) / bd
Subtraction: a/b - c/d = (ad - bc) / bd
Multiplication: a/b × c/d = ac / bd
Division: a/b ÷ c/d = a/b × d/c = ad / bc

methods.name: Simplification (GCD Method)
methods.description: Reduce a fraction to lowest terms by dividing numerator and denominator by their Greatest Common Divisor.

formula.name: GCD Simplification
formula.expression:
Simplified = (a ÷ GCD) / (b ÷ GCD)

GCD found via Euclidean algorithm:
GCD(a, b) = GCD(b, a mod b) until b = 0

methods.name: Mixed Numbers Conversion
methods.description: Converting between improper fractions and mixed numbers (whole number + proper fraction).

formula.name: Mixed Number Conversion
formula.expression:
Improper to Mixed: a/b = (a÷b) + (a mod b)/b
Mixed to Improper: n + a/b = (n×b + a)/b

methods.name: Decimal Conversion
methods.description: Converting fractions to decimals and vice versa. Some fractions produce repeating decimals.

formula.name: Decimal Conversion
formula.expression:
Fraction to Decimal: a/b = a ÷ b

Decimal to Fraction:
0.25 = 25/100 = 1/4
0.333... = 1/3
formula.description: Terminating decimals have denominators with only factors of 2 and 5

methods.accuracy: May introduce rounding errors for repeating decimals
limitations: Many fractions produce infinite repeating decimals

footnotes: Euclidean algorithm: oldest algorithm still in common use (300 BC)
A fraction is in lowest terms when GCD(numerator, denominator) = 1
Fractions with denominators of 2, 4, 5, 8, 10, etc. terminate in decimal form
disclaimer: Fraction calculations are exact when kept in fraction form. Converting to decimal may introduce rounding errors for non-terminating decimals.
